title: Spanda
summary: The subtle vibration or pulsation of consciousness — the eternal self-affirmation of 'I-I'.
intuitiveMeaning: Between waking up and falling asleep, between inhaling and exhaling, between one thought and the next — there is a subtle pulse, the delicate throb of being alive. That pulse, when recognized as the very substance of consciousness, is spanda.
explanation: Spanda is not a movement in space or time but the intrinsic dynamism of I-consciousness. It is the slightest stirring within the absolute — both the source of all manifestation and the repose of consciousness in its own nature. The Spandaśāstra teaches that this pulsation is the very life of consciousness, the eternal self-affirmation 'aham aham' (I-I). It is not a temporal event but the timeless rhythm of self-awareness. Every cognition, every perception, every moment of awareness is a pulsation of spanda. To recognize this is to recognize oneself as the universal subject.

plateHotspots.label: The pulse of awareness
plateHotspots.panelContent: Your own awareness is not static — it pulses. Thoughts arise and dissolve. Attention moves. Awareness itself remains, but its content vibrates. That vibrating is spanda.

plateHotspots.label: The rhythm of light and self-knowing
plateHotspots.panelContent: Spanda is the dynamic relationship between prakāśa and vimarśa — the pulse of illumination and self-possession that is consciousness itself.

sourcePassages.translation: Consciousness, though one, appears contracted as the individual soul. When it pulsates (spanda), it reveals its universal nature.
sourcePassages.commentary: Kṣemarāja comments that the very nature of consciousness is to pulsate — this pulsation is not a quality but its essence.
